suggestion_box:
## Suggestion box — file a grievance about the English

If any English string made you guess, file it. You are the only person who will ever
notice, and a string that made you guess will make the next 25 translators guess too.

File an entry when: the English has more than one plausible reading; a verb or adjective
has no stated object; a word's intended sense is not its most common sense; a term maps
onto a dangerous second sense in your language; a claim in the text looks false or stale;
or the tooling handed you a preferred_translation that is wrong for the context.

Report them in your final message as a JSON array, separate from your prose:

FRICTION: [
  {"key": "<lang key>", "complaint": "<what made you guess, in one sentence>",
   "readings": ["<reading you chose>", "<reading you rejected>"]}
]

An empty array is a fine and useful answer. Do NOT invent entries -- a false one costs a
human's attention. But do not stay quiet to be agreeable either: this channel exists
because real complaints were previously buried in prose and never acted on.

Where it goes and what happens next: the orchestrator copies each entry into
dev/english-friction/<sprint>.json, adds "source": "translator" and "lang": "<your
language code>", and answers it with a "disposition" plus a written "resolution" --
english (the English was rewritten), intent, glossary, dismissed (with the reason), or
refer-to-human. refer-to-human is a real answer and does NOT close the entry: escalating
is not resolving, and it stays visible until Tom rules on it. friction_check.php blocks
the sprint from CLOSING while any entry of yours is unanswered, so filing one is expected
work that the sprint waits on -- not a complaint about the sprint.

lpn.context: Hydraulic head — energy per unit weight of water, expressed as a height of water column. The ROOT concept behind head loss, velocity head, weir head, and gross/net head. A length, never a pressure. Appears as a bare label in Weir Flow (ws_headWaterHeight), Orifice (or_head), and Manning Pipe Flow (mpf_velocity_head). Acceptable English synonyms (translate the concept, not the exact word): energy elevation, hydraulic grade line (HGL).

Several languages split the root by sense: the hydro-power 'fall' sense uses a different word than the pipe 'head' sense (cs spád vs tlaková výška; hr/sr visina·pad vs visina; ro sarcină vs cădere; tr yük vs düşü; ar علو/الارتفاع vs الضغط). lpn.context: A six-line plain-text sidecar file that says where a raster image sits in real-world coordinates and how big one of its pixels is: pixel size in X, two rotation terms, pixel size in Y, and the coordinates of the centre of the top-left pixel. The word "fit" in the English label is the lure — it invites a fitting/adjusting verb while saying nothing about what is fitted, so a translator with no other context reasonably lands on "adjust". THE ENGLISH IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: "Zoom to fit" is an established UI idiom (browsers, PDF viewers, design tools all ship it) and renaming a recognized control costs more than guarding it — this entry plus its avoid array is the guard. Two legitimate conventions exist and both are correct: CAD-faithful (fr "Zoom sur l'étendue", matching AutoCAD's own French/Spanish "Zoom Étendu"/"Zoom Extensión") and plain (tr "Tümünü göster" = show all). Tom chose the PLAIN register for es and pt on 2026-08-08, so 3 of 4 now share the show-everything mental model while fr keeps its correct CAD form. Either register is acceptable for a new language; an adjust-the-zoom reading is not. | [2026-08-13] Sprint 251 wave 4: harvested from the shipped km/my/ur/zh strings, not from agent prose.

lpn.context: The value a field or setting starts with before the user changes it, and the value "Restore defaults" puts back. A software-settings concept, not an engineering one — it appears in suite chrome (calc_defaults, calc_defaults_confirm) and in lpn_ (lpn_settings_defaults "Default inputs", lpn_settings_push_btn, lpn_confirm_restore_defaults). Every language already ships a settled software term for this; the job is to USE that term, not to coin one.
lpn.translation_notes:
Created 2026-08-08 (ROADMAP Task 238) at Tom's request: *"default is a troublesome word. but this is a phrase for which it should be easy to find standard renditions of in any language. so I am hesitant to judge. I just want it to be right."* That is exactly the right instinct and it is why this entry exists: the concept HAS a settled term in every language, so no agent should ever re-derive it, and the risk is not invention but reaching for the wrong sense (financial/legal) or dropping the concept.

Values above are the attested forms already shipping in each language's calc_defaults / calc_defaults_confirm, cross-checked against each other — a language that used the same term in both was taken as self-confirming. Note the low-resource languages (bn, hi, id, ps) legitimately use the English loanword: it IS the standard software term there, and per the defer-to-cultural-standard principle that is correct, not a transliteration defect.

The 2026-08-08 audit of all 26 found 3 real defects, each caught by contradicting its OWN file rather than by outside judgement: ro said only "Reseteaza" on the button while its confirm string said "valorile implicite"; sw said "maadili ya kawaida" (= normal MORALS — "maadili" is ethics, and thamani is the word this file uses for a numeric value in 19 other keys); he had "lerachim breirat hamechdal" where the construct state requires "lerachei". All three fixed. am, my and id were noted as lower-confidence and deliberately left alone rather than guessed at — see Task 238.

lpn.context: Direction toward the water source/supply.
lpn.translation_notes: Hydraulics direction, never software "upgrade" (my file error). tr: memba = upstream, mansap = downstream — a tr file flipped these; pin them.

lpn.context: Direction away from the supply, toward the outlet / last emitter.
lpn.translation_notes: Never software "downgrade". ar: downstream = المصب / أسفل المجرى (a file used المنبعية = source-side, wrong).

lpn.context: In lpn_, a storage node whose water level RISES AND FALLS as it fills and empties: a service reservoir, a standpipe, a clearwell, a farm storage. It is the sibling of a reservoir, which holds a level that never moves. Toolbar label lpn_tool_add_tank; the "T" ID prefix. A steady-state solve cannot tell the two apart at any one instant, which is exactly why the two need different names on screen -- the difference is in what happens NEXT.
lpn.translation_notes: Seeded 2026-08-14 (ROADMAP Task 248) for the tanks/valves/scenarios sprint. Translations are deliberately EMPTY: this entry exists to carry the avoid-list guard into the sprint prompts, not to assert a translation nobody has made yet -- EXCEPT that several languages already coined the word during sprint 146.06 and 251, for the tank lpn_ did not yet have (see the reservoir entry): es depositos, pt tanques, fr reservoirs a niveau variable, ro bazin de acumulare. Prefer continuity with those where they exist. Fill the rest from the sprint output per CLAUDE.md's mandatory glossary write-back. THE THREE LEVEL FIELDS ARE DEPTHS measured up from the tank floor, not elevations on the site datum, and the English labels say "depth" for exactly that reason (Wave 0, 2026-08-14) -- do not translate them with the word your language uses for a water-surface ELEVATION. | [2026-08-14, sprint 316] Harvested from the SHIPPED strings, not from agent prose. All 26 languages kept tank and reservoir as two distinct words -- not one collapsed them, which is the outcome the avoid-list was written for. Several did not coin anything: they reused the word their own file had ALREADY used inside lpn_notes_2_def, the note that used to say tanks were not modelled. That note had been carrying a usable tank word in 26 languages for months, waiting for the element to exist -- so when a cut feature is later built, READ THE STRING THAT ANNOUNCED IT WAS CUT before commissioning a new term. | [2026-08-25, glossary_rendering_census.php] 27 English sites. bn ট্যাংক, cs Nádrž, id Tangki and ps ټانک reach all 27; pt Tanque 26, hr Spremnik 25, ro Bazin 25. What is worth watching is the RESERVOIR word leaking into tank strings, which is exactly the collapse the avoid list was written against: bg резервоар at 5 sites, fr réservoir 4, fa مخزن 4, sr резервоара 4, it serbatoio 3. Small, and none of them has replaced the tank word, but it is the failure mode and it is now measurable. Second renderings that are NOT the reservoir word: es tanque 5 beside Depósito 22, hi टंकी 5 beside टैंक 21.

lpn.context: In lpn_, a LINK -- it sits in the line between two nodes, like a pipe or a pump, not on a node. Five kinds are offered by what they do: a throttle valve (TCV) holding a fixed loss, a pressure reducing valve (PRV), a pressure sustaining valve (PSV) and a flow control valve (FCV). The last three open, close, or partly close by themselves as the water changes.
lpn.translation_notes: Seeded 2026-08-14 (ROADMAP Task 248 phase 2). Use the word a water engineer would use on a distribution main, not the domestic tap word and not the anatomical one. THE FOUR TYPE LABELS ARE ELLIPTICAL IN ENGLISH -- "Pressure reducing (PRV)" with the noun "valve" left out, because they sit in a dropdown already labelled "Valve type". Supply the noun if your language needs it; the parenthesised letters are the international abbreviation and stay as written, in every script and in RTL. Translations deliberately empty; fill from the sprint output. | [2026-08-14, sprint 316] Harvested from the SHIPPED strings, not from agent prose. ps flagged a real cross-prefix split inside its own file: older hw_/bpn_/mphl_ strings use سوپاپ while every shipped lpn_ string uses والو. It followed the narrower incumbent (lpn_) and reported the divergence rather than silently harmonising -- correct, and the reconciliation belongs to a term-centric sweep, not to a calculator sprint. | [2026-08-25, glossary_rendering_census.php] The 2026-08-14 ps finding above, re-measured on the current files: 34 English sites, والو at 31 of them and 50 times in the file, سوپاپ surviving at 3 sites and 3 times. Sprint 459 did not reverse it and the split has narrowed. Nine languages reach all 34 sites (ar, bn, es, fa, fr, hr, id, pt, sr, tr) and most of the rest reach 30 or more. The two low scores are both inflection, not rivalry: ro Vană 17 with vane at 9 more, it Valvola 21 with 13 inflected. am ቫልቭ 16 against the plural ቫልቮች 10 is the same story.

lpn.context: The one number that tells a valve what to do -- and it is A DIFFERENT PHYSICAL QUANTITY FOR EACH TYPE: a PRESSURE for a PRV or PSV, a FLOW for an FCV, and a dimensionless minor-loss coefficient for a TCV. The page therefore shows three different labels in the same slot (lpn_field_valve_setting_pressure / _flow / _loss) rather than one vague "Setting".
lpn.translation_notes: Seeded 2026-08-14 (ROADMAP Task 248 phase 2). The three labels are alternatives for ONE field, so keep them recognisably parallel with each other in your language, the way "Pressure setting" and "Flow setting" are parallel in English. Note that the third one, the throttle valve's loss coefficient, is the SAME KIND OF NUMBER as the pipe minor-loss coefficient k (lpn_field_km) but is a separate field and never appears beside it: a throttle valve is given no minor-loss box, because EPANET ignores one there. Translations deliberately empty; fill from the sprint output.

lpn.context: A property value that belongs to ONE scenario alone and stands in place of the Base value while that scenario is active. A scenario is nothing but a collection of these laid over the shared drawing. The status strip counts them and calls them "Own values" (lpn_scenario_overrides); the per-field checkbox that creates one is "Only in this scenario" (lpn_scenario_override).
lpn.translation_notes: Seeded 2026-08-14 (ROADMAP Task 248 / Task 184) after Wave 0 found the eigenvalue collision in the English label "Own values". The concept a translator wants is the one scenario managers in InfoWater/WaterGEMS use: a value CHANGED IN THIS CASE ONLY. It must read naturally in a very narrow status strip beside the units readout, followed by a count ("Own values: 3"). Note the suite ALREADY uses "local" as a technical term -- "Minor (local) loss" -- so a rendering built on the word "local" collides with an established meaning on the same page and should be avoided. Translations deliberately empty; fill from the sprint output. | [2026-08-14, sprint 316] Harvested from the SHIPPED strings, not from agent prose. THE ENGLISH MOVED BECAUSE OF WHAT THIS SPRINT MEASURED: lpn_scenario_overrides is now 'Custom values', not 'Own values' (Tom: "I love 'custom'. 'Changed' is a little dangerous"). TEN languages independently detected and routed around the eigenvalue calque -- es pt cs it ro uk bg sr de hr -- far wider than the three Wave 0 predicted, and six hit it a second time in lpn_scenario_push_none, a key Wave 0 never flagged. 'Custom' has no calque path into mathematics in any of them, so the trap stops existing rather than being dodged 26 times. THE SECOND FINDING IS THE MORE USEFUL ONE. Clustering the renderings by MEANING split them three ways: 'its own' (13), 'custom/specific/exclusive' (7) and 'CHANGED' (cs hr bg). The third is FALSE here -- a scenario's custom value may be identical to Base's, which scenario-harness.js asserts outright -- and it was invisible in any single language. Being forced off a calque makes a translator CHOOSE a reading, so a divergence in those forced choices measures how many readings the English has. All three were corrected: cs Specificke, hr Svoje, bg Svoi, de Individuelle. ON THE hr/sr APPARENT CONTRADICTION, settled rather than split: 'vlastita vrijednost' IS a documented alternate name for eigenvalue in CROATIAN, while Serbian's dominant term uses a different root (sopstvena), so 'vlastite' is safe in sr and not in hr. Two closely related languages, two genuinely different answers -- do not harmonise them.

lpn.context: The part of a program that computes the answer. In lpn_ there are TWO of them and the UI contrasts them in one sentence: EPANET's own solver, and this suite's built-in solver. Both must be recognisable as the same KIND of thing and distinguishable from each other, so use one noun for both and let the qualifier (EPANET vs built-in) carry the difference.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-13, sprint 252] English was "engine" until Tom changed it to "solver" suite-wide. The evidence that the ENGLISH was the defect, not the translations: 20+ languages were already internally inconsistent, using a correct solver word for the BUILT-IN solver and a motor word for EPANET's -- in the same sentence. sr језгро vs решавач; cs výpočetní jádro vs řešič; id mesin vs penyelesai; hi इंजन vs सॉल्वर; tr motor vs çözücü; ro motorul vs rezolvitorul. Every agent independently resolved it toward the solver word it already had. Russian had avoided the trap from the start (расчётное ядро) and Chinese noted 引擎 unambiguously means a physical engine, so there was no trade-off to make there. Values below are harvested from the shipped lpn_engine_loading strings and verified present in them (bg/ru/uk appear in inflected case).

lpn.context: A drawing of ground elevation and hydraulic grade against distance along a chosen route through the network -- what a civil engineer calls a profile or a long section, as opposed to the plan view the map shows. Use the surveying / civil drawing term of the language, the one that names the sheet a designer reads pipe grades off.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 wave 0] Raised as the highest-traffic string of the profile feature: lpn_profile_menu is one word and names the menu, so a wrong choice mislabels everything under it. English is kept because it is the engineering term of art; the guard belongs here.

lpn.context: The line joining the elevations to which water would rise in open tubes along the pipe: elevation head plus pressure head. Drawn against the ground line on a profile, and the quantity a designer checks minimum pressure against.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 wave 0] The chart legend key lpn_profile_hgl and the prose in lpn_profile_tip must come out as the SAME phrase; they were diverging in English ("Hydraulic grade" vs "hydraulic grade line") and the English has been made to agree. The existing "energy grade line" entry is the neighbouring concept and should use a parallel construction.

lpn.context: EPANET's time series of multipliers: the base demand at a junction is multiplied by the pattern value for the current time step. A pattern belongs to the file and has a name; several junctions may share one.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 wave 0] The word carries the .inp import report (lpn_inp_drop_patterns, lpn_inp_drop_demand_pattern) and the clock, so one rendering must serve all of them.

lpn.context: IMGD is imperial million gallons per day, MGD is US million gallons per day. Both appear in the same flow-unit selector, one row apart.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 wave 0] Raised because the two tokens sit together and neither says which gallon it uses. The user-facing confusability is a separate question for Tom; the translator instruction is simply to leave both tokens alone.

lpn.context: EPANET's pressure breaker valve: it forces a fixed pressure drop between its two ends, in the direction of flow, whatever the flow is. Its siblings in the same selector are PRV, PSV, FCV, TCV and GPV.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 wave 0] English kept: it is EPANET's published element name and identity terms are not renamed. Where the language's water field has no settled phrase, a descriptive rendering ("valve that drops the pressure by a fixed amount") beats reaching for the electrical word.

lpn.context: A project is in one of two modes. A lat/lon project has geographic coordinates and can draw a street map behind it; an XY project is drawn on a plain local grid with no place on the Earth. The names appear in lpn_geomap, lpn_xymap and in the prose of lpn_georef_menu, lpn_georef_tip, lpn_georef_intro, lpn_georef_confirm, lpn_georef_done, lpn_georef_on_map and the four New project rows.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 wave 0] Raised because the names are coined and nothing marked them as coined, so some agents would translate them and others keep them. A per-label synonym would have to be repeated across nine strings; one concept pointer is the right shape.

lpn.context: Which edge or centre of a text label lines up with its anchor point: horizontal alignment left / centre / right, vertical alignment top / middle / bottom. Use the word a word processor or drawing program in the language uses for that control.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 wave 0] The English was wrong and has been fixed (justification -> alignment) in lpn_field_text_align and lpn_field_text_valign. Keep the two labels parallel: one word for both axes.

lpn.context: To leave a value or a whole label off the map because there is not enough room to print it. The Labels box has a column headed with this word (lpn_labels_col_drop), holding a number that orders which value or which test is given up first; the term of art, Priority, lives in that heading's tip. Use the word your language would use for leaving something out of a drawing for want of space.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 Wave 0] The heading replaced an icon and sits in a column about three characters wide, so it must stay very short -- but shortness is exactly what makes the polysemy dangerous: on a hydraulics page a bare "drop" reads first as a drop in head or elevation. Keep it short AND unmistakably about leaving a label off.

lpn.context: One computation of the network over its whole time period: every reporting time from the first to the last, one after another. The button lpn_time_run carries the word alone and must be an IMPERATIVE VERB addressed to the user ("compute it now"); the surrounding strings use the same word as a NOUN ("the start of the run"). Where your language needs different words for the two, use each in its place, and keep the noun consistent across lpn_time_run_tip, lpn_time_run_note and lpn_time_duration.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 Wave 0] EPANET calls this a run, and lpn_time_run_note quotes the button label inside a sentence -- so the word chosen for the button must be the word that appears in that sentence, or the instruction points at a button that is not there.

lpn.context: This suite's plain-English verb for "compute" or "solve": to calculate the flows, pressures and heads of the network. Chosen over "calculate" and "solve" because it is Simple English, and it recurs across the clock strings (lpn_time_run_tip, lpn_time_run_note, lpn_time_running, lpn_time_no_engine). Use your language's ordinary verb for calculating a result -- there is no need for an idiom, and no need to copy the two-word English shape.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 Wave 0] Raised because the phrasal verb is opaque word by word: a reader who parses "work" plus "out" gets exercise, not arithmetic. One rendering should serve all four strings.

lpn.context: The mark between the whole and fractional parts of a number: a dot in English (17.5), a comma in most of Europe, Latin America and elsewhere (17,5). Numbers that appear INSIDE a translated string as EXAMPLES carry the locale's own separator -- write 17,5 where your language writes 17,5. The page accepts both when the user types (js/lpn-patterns.js takes <digits>,<digits> as a decimal), so an example with a comma is a working example, not a broken one. Affects lpn_time_format_tip and lpn_labels_col_decimals_example.
lpn.translation_notes: [2026-08-19, sprint 438 Wave 0] Precedent set for lpn_labels_col_decimals_example, whose whole value is the example 0.000 and which Tom said may become 0,000 where needed. lpn_time_format_tip carries four such examples and nothing in the English says they are localisable.

u.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
u.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed). | [2026-08-25, glossary_rendering_census.php] Counted in the shipped strings, 100 English sites. The glossary rendering is the majority in every language that has one: hr protok 85, sr проток 84, cs průtok 79, ru расход 76, fr débit 75, pt vazão 73, zh 流量 72, bg водно количество 70, km លំហូរ 70, es caudal 69, it portata 69, ar تدفق 69, id debit 69, de Durchfluss 68, tr debi 64, fa دبی 58, he ספיקה 43, uk витрата 43 sites of 99. A second, general water-flowing word still stands at some of the rest: fa جریان 37, id aliran 27, es flujo 25, he זרימה 21, tr akış 20, fr écoulement 15, ar جريان 15, pt escoamento 14, it deflusso 12. NOT ALL OF THOSE ARE DEFECTS -- some English sites really do describe water flowing rather than naming Q, and a count cannot tell the two apart. A worklist for a term-centric sweep, not a correction list.

u.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
u.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

u.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
u.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses. | [2026-08-25, glossary_rendering_census.php] 16 English sites. Most of what a census reports as a rival here is the SIDE SLOPE of a channel, a different concept and correct where it stands: fr talus 5, zh 边坡 5, de böschung 4, ru откос 4, it scarpata 4, ar الجانبي 4. Three are genuine splits inside one language: ur ships ڈھلان at 14 sites while this entry holds ڈھلوان, used at 1; hi ships ढलान 10 against ढाल 5; ps ships میل 9 against شیب 6. ro is a diacritic split only -- pantă here, panta at 4 sites.

keys_to_translate.lpn_result_water_age_tip: How long the water reaching this point has been in the system. There is no standard number to compare it against, so read it as a measurement and judge it yourself.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_source_share_tip: A source trace reports this share: of the water reaching this point, how much of it came from the trace node.
keys_to_translate.lpn_georef_backdrop_unrotated: The background image was moved and resized with the model, but it could not be rotated. Use Background image > Move to line it up.
keys_to_translate.lpn_georef_twopt_tip: Place the model exactly, when you already know where two points on your drawing really are. Click one of them, type its latitude and longitude, then do the same for a second point. The place, the size and the turn all follow from those two. Press this button again to stop picking.
keys_to_translate.lpn_georef_twopt_pick1: Click a point on your drawing whose latitude and longitude you know.
keys_to_translate.lpn_georef_twopt_pick2: Now click a second known point, as far from the first one as you can.
keys_to_translate.lpn_georef_twopt_same: That is the point you picked first. Pick a different one.
keys_to_translate.lpn_georef_twopt_done: The model now sits on the two points you gave. Check it, then press Keep this placement.

keys_to_translate.lpn_find_conn_noopensource: No open path to a source

keys_to_translate.lpn_find_q_err_dot: Put a dot between what to search and its property, like Junction.ID

keys_to_translate.lpn_find_q_err_op: Not a condition for {prop}: {w}. Try one of: {list}

keys_to_translate.lpn_profile_edit_tap: Drag any point on the path to move it. Tap a point you added to take it off.

keys_to_translate.lpn_profile_missing: {name} names nodes that are not in this project: {ids}
keys_to_translate.lpn_new_coords_tip: An xy project is a model on any coordinates other than lat/lon. A lat/lon project has geographic coordinates, so a street map or satellite picture can be drawn behind it and node elevations can be read from the terrain. An xy project can be converted to lat/lon with File > Import xy to lat/lon.
keys_to_translate.lpn_new_place_tip: Optional. Type a town, a street or a landmark and the new map opens there. The words you type go to OpenStreetMap's place-name service, which asks your permission the first time. Leave it empty and the map opens on the whole world.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_rules: This file has rule-based controls. They are not applied here, so the pipes, pumps and valves they name stay at the state written in the file. The rules themselves are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_energy: This EPANET file includes pumping cost modelling data. This page does not work out energy or cost, so nothing here uses those numbers. They are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_tags: This file gives tags to some of its junctions, pipes or other assets. There is nowhere on this page to see a tag or change one yet. The tags are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_report: This file holds EPANET's own settings for the reports it prints. This page shows its answers in its own way, so nothing here uses them. They are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_sections: This file holds a part that this page does not read at all. Nothing here uses it. It is kept whole, and it is written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_quality_options: This file states EPANET water quality options: Quality, which names what to follow through the pipes, and two settings that go with a chemical, Relative diffusivity and Quality tolerance. Water age and trace are worked out here; a chemical is not, so those two settings are kept without being used. All of them are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_inp_drop_file_options: This file names another file beside it: Map, which holds coordinates, or Hydraulics, which holds hydraulics already worked out. This page cannot open either, so the lines are kept as they are and written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_not_converged_drawn: The solve did not converge. These numbers are the last try, not an answer. Do not use them.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_not_converged_error: It stopped after {trials} trials at a relative error of {error}, against an accuracy of {accuracy}.
keys_to_translate.lpn_scenario_mark_tip: Ringed: this element holds a value that belongs to the scenario {name} alone.
keys_to_translate.lpn_scenario_overrides_tip: Each of those values is marked on the map with an amber ring. Switch to Base to see the drawing without them.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_emitter_exponent_tip: The power in the sprinkler and leak law, flow = coefficient x pressure to this power. It only changes the answer where a node has an emitter, which for now means a network read from an EPANET file.
keys_to_translate.lpn_elev_dem_sample_tip: Reads the elevation of the DEM at this node and shows it below for review before changing the current entry. The horizontal DEM resolution is about 30 m for most of the Earth, and finer where better data exists.
keys_to_translate.lpn_elev_dem_use_tip: Puts the elevation of the DEM at this node into the Elevation box above, replacing what is there. It reads the DEM first if it has not been read yet. One Undo puts it back.
keys_to_translate.lpn_elev_dem_none: The DEM gave no height for this node.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_elev_source_tip: Where a new node gets its elevation. The land surface is read from Mapbox DEM, which is about 30 m across on most of the Earth and finer where better data exists.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_accuracy_tip: How close the solver has to get before it stops, measured as the flow still changing from one try to the next. A smaller number is more exact and takes longer. Both solvers read this one box, and each measures that change against a different total: the built-in solver against the sum of the demands, EPANET against the sum of the link flows. Left empty, this page tries far harder than EPANET does on its own.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_specific_gravity_tip: The weight of the fluid compared with water. It changes the pressures a gauge would read, not the flows.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_viscosity_tip: The viscosity of the fluid compared with water at 20 degrees Celsius. It only changes the answer under the Darcy-Weisbach method.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_trials_tip: How many times the solver may try before it gives up on a network that will not settle.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_unbalanced_tip: What to do with a network that has used up its trials and still has not settled. Keeping on allows the extra trials below, which often settles it; stopping reports the last try as it stands, which is close but not solved. Only the EPANET solver reads this box. The built-in solver always stops and marks the answer as unsettled.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_unbalanced_trials_tip: How many further trials to allow after the maximum above is used up, before the last try is reported. Only the EPANET solver reads this box.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_head_error_tip: An additional test the solver must pass before it stops: the largest head any one pipe is still out by. Zero, the usual value, means do not test it. Only the EPANET solver reads this box.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_flow_change_tip: An additional test the solver must pass before it stops: the maximum change in any one pipe's flow from one try to the next. Zero, the usual value, means do not test it. Only the EPANET solver reads this box.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_damp_limit_tip: The accuracy at which the solver begins taking smaller steps, which can settle a network that is swinging back and forth. Zero, the usual value, means it never does. Only the EPANET solver reads this box.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_demand_multiplier_tip: One scale on every demand in the network at once. Use it to ask what the system does at more or less than today's use. It does not change the numbers you typed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_leader_snap_tip: When you drag a label away from what it names, the line back to it is pulled onto the nearest round angle if you drag close to one. Keep dragging and it lets go, so any angle is still available. Off drags freely, which is what this page has always done.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_quality_track_tip: Choose what the run should follow through the pipes: how long the water has been in the system, or where it came from. Neither one asks you for any other number.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_quality_source_tip: The point whose water is followed. Every other point then shows the share of its water that came from here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_quality_chemical: A chemical this file names (kept, not worked out)
keys_to_translate.lpn_quality_needs_run: Water quality is carried along the pipes over time, so it needs the EPANET engine and a total run time. Set a Total run time under Time, then press Run.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_demand_tip: The flow this node draws at the time step shown: the total of base demands multiplied by their patterns. Worked out, not typed, so it changes with the clock and cannot be edited.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_demand_category_tip: Name or description of the category.
keys_to_translate.lpn_demand_add_tip: Add another demand at this junction, with its own base demand, pattern and description. The demands add up.
keys_to_translate.lpn_terrain_will_ids: These are the nodes that will be filled in: {ids}
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_menu_tip: Test every junction: how much can it deliver while it still holds its residual pressure, and does drawing the required flow there create unacceptable drawdown anywhere else?
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_intro: Each junction in turn is asked to draw a fire flow on top of the demand it already has. Nothing in your project is changed; the whole run is made on a copy.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_scope_tip: Choose the set before you run. Testing every junction in a large system can take minutes.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_no_junctions: This project has no junctions yet, so there is nothing to test.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_no_selection: No junction is selected. Choose one on the map, or test every junction.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_required_tip: The flow required by your code or your fire authority at a hydrant. One junction at a time is tested against this same number.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_residual_tip: 20 psi is the AWWA M31 and NFPA 291 convention for available fire flow.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_design: Effect on the rest of the system
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_design_tip: A separate question from whether the junction can deliver the flow: with that flow drawn there, does anything else fall below its minimum pressure or run too fast? Choosing to check it costs no extra calculation.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_design_all: Every other junction and every pipe
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_minpressure_tip: A junction that falls below this while another one is drawing its fire flow is reported as a design issue.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_maxvelocity_tip: A pipe running above this while a fire flow is drawn is reported as a design issue.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_accounting: Fire flow is drawn at the junction itself. That is the method used here, and it is the usual one. The hydrant, its lateral, and its nozzle are not modelled, so a real hydrant delivers less than the flow shown here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_engine_native: This is worked out with the built-in solver.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_engine_epanet: This is worked out with the EPANET engine.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_engine_cost: Available fire flow is a search, so the whole network is solved about sixteen times for every junction tested. A large system takes minutes. You can stop it at any time and keep what it has already worked out.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_steady: Only the current time step is tested. Fire flow is normally added to maximum day demand.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_stopped: Stopped after {done} of {total} junctions. What is below is what had already been worked out.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_stale: The drawing changed, so the fire flow results were cleared. Run it again.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_summary: {pass} passing, {fail} failing, {design} with a design issue.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_design_none: Nothing in the chosen set was drawn down by any junction tested.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_design_off_note: The effect on the rest of the system was not checked in this run.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_iso: ISO credits a single hydrant with at most {flow}. That credit limit has not been applied to any number here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_err_at_rest: Already below the residual with nothing drawn
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_err_solve: The solver reported an error and gave no answer.
keys_to_translate.lpn_ff_err_unknown: No answer, and the reason given is {id}

keys.lpn_result_source_share_tip: A source trace reports this share: of the water reaching this point, how much of it came from the trace node.
keys.lpn_georef_backdrop_unrotated: The background image was moved and resized with the model, but it could not be rotated. Use Background image > Move to line it up.

keys.lpn_georef_twopt_same: That is the point you picked first. Pick a different one.
keys.lpn_georef_twopt_done: The model now sits on the two points you gave. Check it, then press Keep this placement.

keys.lpn_find_conn_noopensource: No open path to a source

keys.lpn_replace_asked: Asked for {n}. The answer is on its way.
keys.lpn_profile_edit_tip: Change one end of the path, or take one node off it, without drawing the whole path again.
